title: Decoding the impact of isolation window selection and QuantUMS filtering in DIA-NN for DIA quantification of peptides and proteins.
projectDescription: Proteomic studies using Data Independent Acquisition (DIA) have gained momentum in all fields of biology. Search engines are evolving to keep up with the latest developments in instrument technology. DIA-NN is the most popular software for DIA analysis under academic use license. The QuantUMS algorithm in DIA-NN improves quantification quality control by calculating three scores (Protein Group MaxLFQ Quality, Empirical Quality, and Quantity Quality) that assess the agreement between MS1 ​​and MS2 features. Here, we show that applying specific cutoffs to these scores can significantly impact results. To enable you to make a more informed decision about what represents a reasonable tradeoff (identification and quantification), we evaluated the impact of different combinations of the scores on data acquired using different isolation windows using a mixture of two-species with known ratio. We compared six different versions of DIA-NN and found high reproducibility across versions, except for version 1.9. We show that filtering by QuantUMS scores removes proteins with low abundance and high coefficients of variation. Finally, we develop the QC4DIANN Shiny application in R language for interactive quality control automation.
sampleProcessingProtocol: A two-species mixture was prepared in a known ratio to investigate accuracy in quantification. Mix A was composed of 200 ng/µL of HeLa peptide standard (Pierce) and 100 ng/µL of yeast peptide standard (Pierce). Mix B was composed of 200 ng/µL of HeLa peptides and 300 ng/µL of yeast peptides. The mixtures were injected into the Vanquish Neo UPLC system equipped with a PepMap Neo Trap cartridge precolumn (300 µm x 5 mm, C18) and a PepMap Neo analytical column (75 µm x 150 mm, 2 µm C18, 100 Ä). A 90 min gradient was used starting from 5% to 30% buffer B (80% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid) in buffer A (0.1% formic acid in water) at 300 nL/min for 70 min, 30% to 40% buffer B at 300 nL/min for 7 min, 40% to 99% buffer B at 300 nL/min for 12 min. The Vanquish Neo system was coupled to an Orbitrap Exploris 480 mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific) via a NanoSpray Flex ionization source. The instrument was operated in DIA mode collecting full MS from 400 to 900 m/z, in profile mode with a maximum injection time of 50 ms. Precursor selection was performed with isolation windows of 10, 6, 4 or 2 m/z, with maximum injection time of 50 ms, in a range of 400 to 900 m/z. Scans were acquired with a resolution of 30,000 FWHM at 400 Da with an AGC target of 1,000% in centroid mode. The default charge state was selected as +2. Fragmentation was performed using two collision energies (stepped collisional energy) selected as 28% and 32%. The samples were injected in a block randomized scheme containing replicates representative of all isolation windows to decrease the impact of systematic error.
dataProcessingProtocol: The Thermo raw files were converted to mzML using the MSConvert (Proteowizard) application with the peak picking filter activated. The files were analyzed in the DIA-NN search engine version 2.0.2 (19) with the fused reference banks (UniProtKB) of Homo sapiens and Saccharomyces cerevisiae containing only canonical sequences. The common contaminants were added to the FASTA file from the DIA-NN search engine cRAP-bank. As variable modifications, N-terminal acetylation (+42.0106) and methionine oxidation (+15.9949) were selected, while carbamidomethylation of Cys (+57.0214) was selected as fixed modification. Trypsin was established as protease specificity, assuming one cleavage error, peptide size from 7 to 35 amino acid residues and precursor scan range of 400 to 900 m/z. The FDR was set at 1% in QuantUMS high accuracy mode with calibration mass tolerance automatically selected by the software. The report.parquet file generated by DIA-NN search was loaded in R session using the following filter combination Lib.PG.Q.Value ≤ 0.01, Lib.Q.Value ≤ 0.01, and PG.Q.Value ≤ 0.01. Unless otherwise mentioned, the QuantUMS scores were set to zero. To extract the protein abundance matrix using MaxLFQ intensities as metric, the diann library for R was used setting the Protein.Names as the id.header and Genes.MaxLFQ.Unique as the quantity.header. Differential abundance was evaluated using limma with least squares method and Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons.
